subject: Priority Account: AuroraCommerce recovery pact and owner ledger
messages:
From: Sam Leong <sam.leong@auroracommerce.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.nair@auroracommerce.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Major production degradation this morning (high latency + errors)

Priyom —

We started seeing request latencies spike across our cart/checkout routes around 01:40 UTC; error rate also rose to ~6% and throughput dropped as retries queued. This is impacting checkout conversions across three regions. Our SREs opened a bridge and are asking for the latest mitigation ETA. Can you confirm you have a post-incident plan and when we’ll get an RCA and timeline for fixes?

I can join a bridge immediately if useful. Please escalate to whoever owns priority accounts — we need a firm path to restoration and a list of owners for each corrective action.

— Sam
Sam Leong
Head of Engineering | AuroraCommerce
Attachments: none

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sam Leong <sam.leong@auroracommerce.com>
Cc: priya.nair@auroracommerce.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major production degradation this morning (high latency + errors)

Sam —

Thanks for flagging and sorry about the impact. We stood up an incident bridge at 01:48 UTC and applied a multi-stage mitigation: 1) temporarily reduced batching window for the checkout model shard to meet latency SLOs; 2) enabled prefix KV-caching on the hot path; 3) diverted lower-priority traffic to a cheaper model variant to free up GPU capacity. That cut error rate back to ~0.9% and restored latency for most requests by 02:20 UTC.

We’re drafting an RCA and a concrete remediation plan now. I’ve looped in Neha (account lead) for ownership and Jordan (CS exec) for exec-communications. Expect the initial RCA doc and action ledger in ~36 hours; we’ll include timelines and owners for each corrective item and a customer verification checklist.

Can you confirm whether Aurora needs an embargoed readout (exec-only) or the full doc by EOD Thursday? Also attaching a brief token-usage snapshot for the recovery window — let me know if you want deeper raw logs.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: token-usage-snapshot-20271018.csv

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AuroraCommerce incident — immediate next steps and owners

Team —

Summary (from bridge): transient surge in very long sequences led to inefficient kernel selection and degraded batching efficiency for the primary checkout model. Secondary contributor: a KV cache miss storm on a promotion-heavy checkout flow. Actions we committed on call:

- Short-term (owners & ETA):
  * Priyom: complete incident timeline + attach token usage by 10/20 10:00 PDT (DONE: snapshot attached).
  * Kimberly: performance tuning on kernel selection heuristics and a fallback to the low-latency kernel by 10/21 EOD (OWNER).
  * Marissa: coordinate canary with Aurora SRE and validate rollback window; target canary for 10/22 08:00 PDT (OWNER).
  * Neha: owner for customer communications and exec readout; deliver exec summary by 10/21 12:00 PDT.

- Mid-term (architecture / platform):
  * Re-evaluate batching policy thresholds for checkout routes under promotion bursts (investigation ticket HS-37492).
  * Add KV-cache warmup guidance for customers with high-promotions cadence.

Please confirm if owners above are ok. Jordan — please advise if we should route any of this to engineering leaders for headcount or infra commit asks during the exec readout.

Neha Kapoor
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sam Leong <sam.leong@auroracommerce.com>, priya.nair@auroracommerce.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: AuroraCommerce incident — immediate next steps and owners

All —

This looks good. Two asks from the exec side:

1) Neha — include a one-pager exec readout (impact metrics, remediation status, risk of recurrence, and recommended customer mitigation) for Aurora’s CTO and our VP of Sales. Keep it to one page with a clear acceptance criteria.

2) Kimberly — if kernel fallback requires a config change that could impact other tenants, document rollback and blast radius in the RCA. If you need dedicated infra time, we should surface the ask tomorrow; I’ll backstop with sales leadership.

Sam/Priya — we’ll run the canary on 10/22 08:00 PDT and follow up that morning with the verification checklist. We’ll also offer a 30-minute exec readout window if you want to take it then or schedule for 10/22 13:00 PDT.

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sam Leong <sam.leong@auroracommerce.com>, priya.nair@auroracommerce.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident packet: RCA + corrective actions (canary complete)

Sam / Priya —

Attached is the post-incident packet (aurora_rca_v1.pdf). Quick summary:

- Incident window: 2027-10-18 01:38 — 2027-10-18 03:05 UTC. Peak error-rate: 6.1% (checkout routes).
- Root causes: inefficient kernel selection on long sequences + KV-cache storm on promotion-heavy flows.
- Immediate mitigations taken: temporary reduced batching window; prefix KV-cache enablement; traffic diversion to a latency-optimized model variant.
- Canary: completed 10/22 08:00 PDT against 2% of traffic; verification checklist passed (99.2th percentile latency within SLA, error-rate <0.5% for checkout).

Corrective actions and owners (with target dates):
  1) Kernel-selection fallback & config controls — Kimberly Park — target 2027-10-21 (deployed 2027-10-21 19:30 PDT).
  2) KV-cache warmup documentation + SDK helper — Priyom Das — target 2027-10-26.
  3) Batching policy tuning for promotion spikes (platform ticket HS-37492) — Engineering TBD, customer-impact assessment 2027-11-02.
  4) Monthly verification runbook for Aurora (two-week smoke + surge simulation) — Marissa Cole — draft due 2027-11-05.

Neha will follow up with an exec one-pager and a DocuSign acceptance that lists closure criteria (canary verification + 2 weeks of stable telemetry). We offered a goodwill credit for the affected billing period and a free upgrade window on Dedicated tiers for a limited test.

Please reply with any clarifications — we’ll treat this as the canonical ledger and update the DocuSign once Aurora confirms.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_rca_v1.pdf
